reviewed_by: Claude Code, hardening deploys after the 2026-11-20 d223a68 promotion needed an operator to restart it
reason: Every deploy reported target_execution and every handoff as uncertain and needed reruns. Root cause (independently confirmed): RuntimeManagement.dispatch returned the full deployment status for promote_api, target_execution, handoff and rollback_code, and the operation receipt is bounded at 64 KiB; with 709 projects the status is ~167 KB, so the committed effect was reported as an uncertain ValueError. Core now returns a bounded summary (revision, versions, health, and the handoff's own project row). Deployer: Core reads time out after 60 s and are retried (deployment status is slow during handoffs; a 20 s timeout ended runs); waiting for the new host waits out a degraded status while the old API worker drains; a project whose only blockers are idle harness sessions Core cannot restore is stopped without waiting out the grace; promotion retires unowned workers of older versions once every project runs the target (one left behind would hold the next release at execution staged); superseded-manual reconciliation accepts succeeded promote/target receipts. Selected: runtime management (busy-host target and handoff receipts fail on main with the live symptom) and operations suites, the new read-retry tests, staged deployer (immediate stop for idle-only blockers, grace kept for others, leftover retirement), deploy-resume and deployer protocol suites.
exclusions: tests/test_simulation_host_activation.py passes locally (including the new degraded-wait case) except the onefile identity case that fails on unmodified main here; tests/v3/test_supervisor.py and test_runtime_coordination.py pass locally and are unchanged. PostgreSQL variants run in CI. No staging replay: the busy-host status is reproduced in the runtime management tests with a 700-project status.
